Subject: VAT on GCP co-sell invoice — need confirmation

Hi Soojin,

Quick question on how invoicing shows up when we buy via GCP marketplace with a co-sell path: our procurement team expects a single monthly invoice from Google that includes both the marketplace fee and the partner charge, but our finance team says they need Redwood-originated line items for VAT reclaim in the EU. I attached a sample marketplace invoice (what Acme received) — you can see only a gross charge and a VAT line applied by Google. We need to know whether we can provide a net invoice from Redwood for our internal VAT reclaim and what paperwork (W-8/W-9 or VAT registration proof) we should collect.

Quick summary from marketplace ops / prior deals (long version below):

- GCP marketplace (co-sell) normally operates with Google as the billing intermediary. For many customers in EU, Google collects VAT and appears as the seller-of-record on the invoice. That means the single invoice Acme received listing a gross charge + VAT line is typical.
- Redwood is usually paid by Google (marketplace payout) rather than issuing a customer-facing invoice in that flow. So we can't always issue a parallel "customer invoice" that Google will accept as official for the same transaction.
- However, some customers require Redwood-originated documentation for VAT reclaim or internal chargeback. For EU customers with a valid VAT ID and reverse-charge eligibility, we can provide a supplemental invoice/statement that breaks out Redwood's net portion and references the marketplace transaction ID — this is labeled as "supplemental partner statement" (not a duplicate tax invoice).

What to collect from Acme:
- EU VAT number (VIES-validated) and company registration name/address.
- A signed confirmation that they purchased via GCP marketplace and consent to receiving a partner statement.

What to send back:
- Supplemental partner statement (PDF): Redwood net line items, our tax reg number, and a reference to GCP invoice id. Mark clearly: "This document is provided for partner billing and chargeback only — not a replacement of marketplace invoice."
- If legal requires it, we can include a short clause that we are not the seller-of-record for the marketplace transaction.

AWS/Azure notes (differences):
- AWS: AWS Marketplace sometimes supports partner-originated invoices via the Seller Private Offers path where partner can be seller-of-record depending on the setup; in many co-sell deals AWS is still seller-of-record.
- Azure: similar variability; Microsoft has specific ISV seller options that can lead to partner invoices in some cases.

Action items: Marcus — can finance produce a one-page partner statement PDF template that we can populate programmatically (deal id, marketplace invoice id, Redwood tax id, net amount)? Priya — flag for legal review (short statement language).

Lower-level detail / tax forms:
- W-8 / W-9 only matter for US tax withholding and payout remittance to Redwood; for EU VAT reclaim by Acme they are irrelevant. For US customers buying via marketplace, we still need appropriate tax forms for payout compliance (W-9 for US entities or W-8BEN-E for foreign entities).

I'll attach a quick set of notes and a sample partner statement template.

-Karthik
Head of GTM Operations, Redwood Inference

Following up with finance feasibility and the partner-statement template. See attached sample PDF we will use for Acme — it includes: Redwood net line, marketplace invoice id, Redwood VAT/Tax ID, sentence that Google is seller-of-record, and a sign-off line. We will:

1) Generate the partner-statement as a non-tax invoice (hosted on Drive with link and sent to customer).
2) For EU customers with reverse-charge, we will include the phrase "VAT reverse charge applies — customer to account for VAT under local law" when Acme's VAT id validates.
3) Keep internal mapping: marketplace invoice id -> Redwood payout id -> Redwood internal invoice stub for accounting.

Marcus asks: do we want the partner-statement to include gross-to-net math (showing Google gross, Redwood net) or just Redwood net? My recommendation: show both numbers with explicit labels so customer's finance team has easier chargeback reconciliation.

Subject: Re: VAT on GCP co-sell invoice — need confirmation

Hi Anna — thanks for the example and patience. Short answer: Google is usually the seller-of-record on GCP marketplace; they will issue the official invoice and apply VAT. What we can provide is a Redwood partner statement that lists Redwood's net portion, references the GCP invoice id, and includes our tax/VAT id and a short legal note that Google is seller-of-record. This should satisfy most EU customers' chargeback processes, but it is not a replacement for Google's invoice for VAT reclaim in every jurisdiction.

Next steps:
- Can Acme share the VIES-validated VAT ID and confirm Ireland as the billing country?
- Marcus will send the partner-statement PDF (example attached) that includes both gross and net breakdowns.
- Priya will validate the wording for the legal note.

If Acme requires Redwood to be seller-of-record (i.e., a direct Redwood invoice only), we can discuss alternative procurement routes (private offer / direct contract) but that will change the co-sell flow and likely affect pricing and procurement lead time.

Anna — tagging the Google billing alias in case there are marketplace-specific nuances we missed: GCP Marketplace Billing <gcp-billing@google.com>.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Partner Sales, Redwood Inference
